questions.text: In the given matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1&2 \\ 0& 1 & 0\\ 1&2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], one of the eigenvalues is 1. The eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue 1 are
questions.solution:
[latex]A-I=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1&2\\0&0&0\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}[/latex]

- Row 1: [latex]-[/latex]y + 2z = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y = 2z
- Row 3: x + 2y = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] x = [latex]-[/latex]4z

z = 1 gives ([latex]-[/latex]4, 2, 1).

Answer: [latex]\alpha(-4,2,1)[/latex]

questions.text:
Perform the following operations on the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4&45 \\ 7& 9& 105\\ 13&2 & 195 \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
(i) Add the third row to the second row
(ii) Subtract the third column from the first column.
The determinant of the resultant matrix is___________.
questions.solution:
Adding a row to another row, or subtracting a column from another column, does not change the determinant.

In the original matrix the third column is 15 times the first (45 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 3, 105 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 7, 195 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 13), so the determinant is 0.

Answer: 0

questions.text:
Let [latex]f(x)=x^{-(1/3)}[/latex] and A denote the area of the region bounded by f(x) and the x-axis, when x varies from -1 to 1. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
I) f is continuous in [-1,1]
II) f is not bounded in [-1,1]
III) A is nonzero and finite
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)=x^{-1/3}[/latex] blows up at x = 0, so it is not continuous (I false) and not bounded (II true) on [[latex]-[/latex]1, 1].

Area = [latex]2\int_0^1x^{-1/3}dx=2\cdot\frac32=3[/latex], finite and non-zero (III true).

Answer: II and III only

questions.text: The secant method is used to find the root of an equation f(x)=0. It is started from two distinct estimates [latex]x_{a}[/latex] and [latex]x_{b}[/latex] for the root. It is an iterative procedure involving linear interpolation to a root. The iteration stops if [latex]f(x_{b})[/latex] is very small and then [latex]x_{b}[/latex] is the solution. The procedure is given below. Observe that there is an expression which is missing and is marked by ?. Which is the suitable expression that is to be put in place of ? so that it follows all steps of the secant method?
questions.solution:
The secant line through [latex](x_a,f(x_a))[/latex] and [latex](x_b,f_b)[/latex] crosses the x-axis at:

[latex]x_t=x_b-\frac{(x_b-x_a)f_b}{f_b-f(x_a)}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]x_b-(x_b-x_a)f_b/(f_b-f(x_a))[/latex]
